results.title: NAGRAT calls for rigorous system to regulate early BECE, describes two-year ban as harsh
results.content: The National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) has called for a rigorous system to regulate the early progression of pupils to higher classes, describing the Education Ministry’s two-year ban on early BECE candidates as too harsh.

results.title: Three arrested as police intercept truck carrying 2,349 rounds of ammunition
results.content: The Eastern Regional Police Command has arrested three persons after intercepting a KIA truck carrying 2,349 rounds of ammunition at Akuse Junction. The ammunition, comprising 800 rounds of G3 ammunition, 1,250 AAA cartridges and 299 rounds of 9mm pistol ammunition, was concealed in a green sack beneath assorted goods and alcoholic beverages. In a statement issued on Thursday, November 26, 2026, the Police Public Affairs Unit said officers received intelligence on Wednesday, November 25, that a KIA truck suspected of carrying contraband goods from Accra towards Bimbilla was approaching the Kpong area. Acting on the information, personnel from Operation Motherland, together with officers from the Akuse District Command, intercepted the vehicle, with registration number GS 4050-12, at Akuse Junction.

results.title: ‘Gifted pupils’ exemption is an afterthought’ – NPP on BECE ban
results.content: The Co-chair of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Education Committee, Dr Prince Hamid Armah, has described the Education Minister’s decision to make room for exceptionally gifted pupils under the two-year examination ban as an “afterthought”.

results.title: Ghana Publishing Company forgoes 2025 dividend payment despite recording GH¢16.9m profit, opts to reinvest profits
results.content: The Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) will not pay dividends to its sole shareholder for the 2025 financial year, opting instead to reinvest its profits in the modernisation of its printing equipment. The decision comes despite the company's strong financial performance, which saw revenue increase by 20% to GH¢72.9 million and profit after tax rise to GH¢16.9 million. Board Chairman, Mathew Lawer Teye, announced the decision at the company's Annual General Meeting on Thursday, November 26, 2026. "After careful deliberation, the Board has decided not to recommend the payment of a dividend for the 2025 financial year, despite the strong financial performance," he stated.

results.title: GRIDCo restores Aboadze-Anwomaso transmission line after damage by illegal chainsaw operators
results.content: The Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) has restored the 330kV Aboadze-Anwomaso transmission line to operation after completing repairs to damage caused by a fallen tree. In a statement issued on Thursday, November 26, 2026, the company said the line was damaged a day earlier after illegal chainsaw operators felled a tree onto the transmission infrastructure. GRIDCo said repair works were completed at approximately 12:07 p.m. on Thursday, restoring the line to full operation. Following the incident, the company appealed to the public to help protect electricity transmission infrastructure by avoiding illegal chainsaw operations and other activities near transmission lines and associated facilities.

results.title: EPA says mining and land reclamation require environmental assessment and permits
results.content: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has outlined the legal frameworks governing environmental protection, mining activities and the restoration of degraded lands and water bodies in Ghana.

results.title: DigiPlas-GH seeks to improve plastic waste recovery and trading
results.content: A digital marketplace designed to connect plastic waste collectors, aggregators, recyclers and manufacturers has been introduced in Ghana to improve trading and strengthen plastic waste recovery. The DigiPlas-GH platform is expected to provide a virtual marketplace where stakeholders can buy and sell recyclable materials, access market opportunities and coordinate activities across the plastic waste value chain. The platform will also help track the volume and quality of plastic waste collected and channelled into recycling, providing data to assess the impact of recovery activities. results.title: Crocodile Matchets (Ghana) Limited unveils upgraded machete with improved durability, comfort
results.content: Crocodile Machets (Ghana) Limited has launched an improved version of its Crocodile Machet 410, popularly known as Kotokrodu, incorporating changes aimed at making the farming tool more comfortable, durable and efficient. The company says the upgraded 58mm Pattern 410 machets addresses concerns raised by farmers and other customers about the handle, blade thickness and protective coating. Speaking at the launch, Managing Director of Crocodile Machetes Ghana Ltd, Sjoerd Grueter, said the improvements followed feedback from farmers who had called for a machete with a bigger head and thicker tip to make farm work easier. “We have been receiving feedback from farmers over the years. They expressed the desire for us to produce a machete with a bigger head and a thicker tip to improve their farming activities,” he said.

results.title: Ghana Schools Project equips Madonna Catholic Clinic with a surgical theatre and medical equipment
results.content: Residents of Besease and surrounding communities are expected to have improved access to surgical and emergency healthcare following the handover of a modern surgical theatre and medical equipment to Madonna Catholic Clinic. The intervention by the Ghana Schools Project is expected to strengthen the clinic’s capacity to manage surgical cases, provide emergency obstetric care and reduce referrals to other health facilities. For more than 30 years, Madonna Catholic Clinic has provided healthcare services to Besease and neighbouring communities. However, the absence of a surgical theatre and specialised medical equipment limited its ability to undertake certain procedures, forcing patients requiring urgent surgical attention to seek care elsewhere. results.title: DHL highlights growing Africa-Germany trade opportunities, cites 54.6% shipment growth in Ghana
results.content: DHL has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening trade and business connectivity in Sub-Saharan Africa, citing growing opportunities in the Africa-Germany trade relationship.

results.title: EPA’s water framework must deliver tangible results – Volta Regional Minister
results.content: Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, has called for effective implementation of environmental policies, warning against allowing important policy documents to remain on shelves without producing tangible results.

results.title: We cannot bequeath polluted rivers, degraded wetlands to future generations – Volta Regional Minister
results.content: Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, has called for stronger environmental protection measures to safeguard Ghana’s water resources and natural assets for future generations.

results.title: Three arrested with 79 parcels of suspected narcotics in Kumasi
results.content: Police in the Ashanti Region have arrested three people for allegedly possessing suspected narcotic drugs for trafficking following an intelligence-led operation at Krobo Odumasi (K.O.) in Kumasi. The suspects have been identified as Daniel Agboloso, 46, a driver; Joyce Adu, alias Yaa Ampofowaa, 43, a trader; and Agyei Bright, 42, a driver's mate. Officers from the Drug Law Enforcement Unit (DLEU) in Kumasi conducted the operation during which the suspects were intercepted while travelling in a Mercedes-Benz Sprinter bus with registration number AS 3566-20.

results.title: ‘We paid the debt the NPP could not pay’ – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has defended the government's debt management record, saying the National Democratic Congress (NDC) has paid billions of cedis in domestic debt and billions of dollars to Eurobond holders inherited from the previous administration. He made the remarks in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, 2026, during the closing debate on the 2027 Budget Statement, following the government's early buyback of part of the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) bonds due in February 2027. Dr Forson said the government had paid more than GH¢46.5 billion in inherited domestic debt and US$2.1 billion to Eurobond holders, including US$700 million in July. "Together, we have paid over 46.5 billion Ghana cedis to domestic debt we inherited. We have also paid 2.1 billion US dollars to Eurobond holders, including 700 million US dollars in July," he said.

results.title: Trade Minister launches digital platform to tackle trade barriers in Ghana
results.content: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has launched a digital platform to help traders and businesses report trade barriers and track efforts to resolve them.

results.title: Foreign Affairs Ministry cautions Ghanaians against job offers in Iraq, Syria
results.content: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has cautioned Ghanaians seeking employment opportunities in Iraq and Syria, particularly as domestic workers, to exercise extreme caution and verify job offers before travelling to the countries.

results.title: Trade Minister engages DHL, Volkswagen to boost logistics and automotive investment in Ghana
results.content: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has held separate engagements with executives of DHL International and Volkswagen to explore opportunities to strengthen trade facilitation, logistics services and investment in Ghana's automotive industry.

results.title: Black Challenge arrive in Accra to heroes welcome after historic World Cup triumph
results.content: The victorious side received a rousing welcome at the Accra International Airport, with invited guests encouraged to turn up in their Ghanaian jerseys to celebrate the team's remarkable achievement.

results.title: Scientists urge government to invest in Ghana’s endangered indigenous crops
results.content: Scientists at the Crops Research Institute of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, working under a project to preserve Ghana’s minor crops, say now is the time for government to turn an immediate attention to the country’s underutilised and endangered crops.

results.title: ‘We don’t want this to be a fluke’ – Kofi Adams on Black Challenge Amputee World Cup win
results.content: The Black Challenge achieved a historic feat after beating Morocco in the final of the World Cup in Mexico, beating the second African country to also claim the title after Angola.

results.title: Law Class of 1994/96 donates GH¢60,000, computers to Legal Aid Commission for 24-hour call centre
results.content: The Law Class of 1994/96 has donated GH¢60,000 and two desktop computers to the Legal Aid Commission to support the establishment of a 24-hour call centre aimed at expanding access to justice across the country.

results.title: 2027 Budget is a budget of restraint with purpose – Majority Leader
results.content: Majority Leader, James Agalga, has described the 2027 Budget as a “budget of restraint with purpose”, saying it offers Ghana an opportunity to pursue development without placing additional debt burdens on future generations.

results.title: Labour Ministry and GIZ explore employment opportunities for Ghanaian youth in Germany
results.content: The Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment has engaged the German development agency, GIZ, to expand employment opportunities and establish safe migration pathways for Ghanaian youth seeking jobs in Germany.

results.title: Playback: EPA launched water restoration and management framework in Ho
results.content: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) is launching a new framework to guide the restoration and sustainable management of degraded water bodies across the country.

results.title: ‘A promise made is a promise kept’ – Agalga touts $12.7bn reserves
results.content: Majority Leader, James Agalga, has touted Ghana's gross international reserves of $12.7 billion, saying the figure demonstrates the government's delivery on its promise to strengthen the country's external position.

results.title: Children demand stronger action to protect their rights at National Children’s Parliament
results.content: Children from across Ghana have called for stronger action to protect their rights, urging government and stakeholders to translate commitments to their welfare into tangible improvements in their lives.

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Building a culture of ownership and high performance
results.content: High-performing organizations are built by people who understand their responsibilities, take ownership of outcomes and remain committed to delivering results. A culture of ownership develops when employees are empowered to act, managers provide clear direction and leaders consistently reinforce accountability.

results.title: Ghana records average of 100 fire outbreaks weekly – Interior Minister
results.content: Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak has disclosed that Ghana records an average of 100 fire outbreaks every week, with incidents increasing during the peak fire season between October and February.

results.title: ‘This is the people’s budget’ – Agalga defends 2027 budget, rules out new taxes
results.content: Majority Leader James Agalga has defended the 2027 Budget as a “people's budget”, saying it delivers on the government's promises to reduce inflation, borrowing and excessive public spending without introducing new taxes. Contributing to the closing debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, 2026, Agalga said the government would also fund major infrastructure projects without resorting to additional borrowing. "Indeed, it is the people's budget. Let me say that again, this is the people's budget. No new taxes, no borrowing for the Accra-Kumasi Expressway, no borrowing for the Western Corridor Railway Line," he stated.
